tests.protocol: Compile spec and body in an isolated 19c schema. Inspect USER_ERRORS and warnings. Gate: no duplicate declaration errors and no unrelated error declarations.
Compile both declarations and definitions. Call the legacy routine and the new overload with named notation. Test approval and denial and inspect both outputs.
Install in an empty 19c test schema, verify job actions, run each once, inspect USER_SCHEDULER_JOB_RUN_DETAILS, then repeat the upgrade with deliberately stale attributes.
Test absent keys, 0, negative, decimal comma, decimal point, expression text, NULL, and normal values. Verify boundary times against a fixed clock fixture.
Install with only declared prerequisites. Verify compilation and authorized execution. Verify that an unapproved account cannot invoke the worker or read the workflow tables.
Test own session, another ordinary account, protected operator, nested role, NOT_DBA, revoked permission, and proxy access. Gate: every allowed and denied action matches an explicit matrix.
Test direct calls for SYS, an Oracle-maintained non-SYS account, a background session, the caller session, and a protected service; confirm that no engine command is issued.
Use two RAC instances with overlapping SID values and process addresses. Verify exactly one selected identity, correct process, and explicit rejection of incomplete legacy rows.
On RAC, select a remote target and verify the command contains its instance. Test a same-pair local fixture, fractional input, NULL, and a local compatibility call.
Request approval, end the target, create a replacement, then approve. Change eligibility and permissions before approval. Gate: stale or no-longer-allowed targets never reach the engine.
Test several child cursors, idle target, NULL SQL_ID, aged-out cursor and changing SQL. Gate: one target record, nullable diagnostics, deterministic result status.
Execute the same SQL from two sessions, sample its child cursor, and confirm the report labels cumulative cursor values and microseconds rather than target-session elapsed time.
Test IDs 999, 1000, and a larger generated value; inspect returned references. Verify the primary-key constraint and migrate only after duplicate/NULL diagnostics pass.
Simulate ORA-00031 with a worker test double, then test a real managed test session where possible. Verify M is stored, no killed claim is emitted, and reconciliation can advance it.
Feed each engine outcome into direct and confirmation paths. Require identical domain classification. Test unexpected engine error and inspect all returned outputs and persisted states.
Force a constraint error, invalid trigger, missing row, and denied dictionary access. Gate: no engine invocation; original error remains available even when the logger also fails.
Run two simultaneous requests, two approvals, approval versus cancellation, and crash points before/after claim and command. Gate: one claim, no blind repeat, and visible uncertain outcomes.
Create an unrelated uncommitted sentinel update, call each API, then rollback. Verify the stated contract. Test autonomous code against caller-held workflow locks for deadlocks.
Exercise initial denial, repeated denial, each terminal transition, and direct metadata updates. Verify no hidden trigger error and no unauthorized terminal outcome change.
Test exact cutoff, old C, old O, active X, marked M, old E, concurrent approval, and both historical job orders. Gate: no executing request becomes a normal expired request.
Repeat each report and worker path many times, including exceptions. Inspect open-cursor counts and NLS settings. Query every defined state and verify labels and access rules.
Test long usernames, process IDs, many roles, multibyte reason text and SQL longer than 1000 bytes. Verify explicit outcomes and that the helper cannot be mistaken for successful termination.
Test logger off, filter exclusion, table/screen destination, missing config, failing insert, and logger exception handling. Verify domain audit persists and original failures survive logger failures.
Set caller instrumentation, log success and failures, and verify exact restoration. Measure dictionary calls, elapsed latency, autonomous commits and concurrent throughput with logging on/off.
